message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $1914 and four houses on every brown, pink, and orange property. Most other holdings are mortgaged or unmortgaged with no houses. The opponent has only $110 and is in jail for two turns.

The opponent has no get-out-of-jail-free cards and all their properties are mortgaged. I will not build hotels because that returns houses to the bank for them to buy later. I will also avoid unmortgaging or trading cash for monopolies. Any pink or orange roll should bankrupt them. They previously rejected my $100 offer for Boardwalk.

The opponent needs roughly $374 to unmortgage their red properties, but only has $110. I am weighing whether to unmortgage any holdings now that I have $1914.

I cannot build on the light blue monopoly because the bank has no houses left. I also own all three yellow properties, though two are mortgaged.

Unmortgaging the yellow properties would still leave no houses to build. The opponent is already blocked from greens and dark blues, so unmortgaging would only waste cash on rent income while they remain in jail.

The opponent has two jail turns left. If they fail to roll doubles on their third turn, they must pay $50 and leave. Since all their properties are mortgaged, landing there would yield no rent income.

The opponent rolled 6+2 on turn 151 and 2+3 on turn 153. Both were non-doubles. They have two failed jail attempts behind them.

I am calculating the exact rent values for my four-house properties to gauge how much income I can expect if the opponent is forced out of jail.

Even the cheapest four-house rent is $160, well above the opponent's cash. Any of my developed properties would bankrupt them immediately if they land there. They could also hit Chance or Community Chest cards. I will not trade for Boardwalk to complete dark blues because the bank has no houses left.

I will not give the opponent cash. That would only help them survive longer in jail or pay down debts. If they go bankrupt, I inherit all their assets anyway. Mortgaged properties transfer to me, but I must pay 10% interest and can choose whether to unmortgage them.

If the opponent goes bankrupt to me, I would inherit Boardwalk for only $20 in interest plus the $200 mortgage value. That is far cheaper than paying them cash now. Trading any property to them would give them an asset they could mortgage for cash. I will not unmortgage Marvin Gardens or North Carolina because that would break my green monopoly.
